name: Indonesian jaipongan (Sundanese popular)
lineage: Indonesian jaipongan Sundanese popular-music genre developed in 1974 by Gugum Gumbira in Bandung (West Java) as a modernization of the older ketuk tilu Sundanese folk-dance-music. The form incorporates the traditional kendang Sundanese drum-set, gamelan degung metallophone framework, and Sundanese-language vocal repertoire, but with substantially energized faster-tempo rhythmic pulse and assertive female-singer-dancer presentation. The genre became culturally significant during the late-1970s Indonesian-cultural-nationalism period as an alternative to Western-influenced popular music. Distinguished from broader Sundanese gamelan by jaipongan's mid-1970s commercial-popular crystallization and the assertive vocal-and-dance performance register.
